f of x equals x cubed minus five x plus one. Work out f of one. (This is part of showing that f has a solution between zero and one.)
Show that x cubed plus two x minus seven equals zero has a solution between one and two.

f of x equals x cubed plus x minus three has f of (one point two one) equals minus zero point zero one eight and f of (one point two two) equals zero point zero three six (to three decimal places). The solution lies in an interval of width zero point zero one. What is the lower end of this interval? Type it like one point three five.
f of x equals x cubed plus x minus three. Work out f of (one point two five), to three decimal places. Is the solution above or below one point two five?

Key idea: if the terms settle at L, then L fits the rule: L equals ∛(three minus L). Cube both sides: L cubed equals three minus L, so L cubed plus L minus three equals zero. So L is a solution of the original equation. That is why the method works.
Which of these is x cubed plus x minus three equals zero rearranged into the form x equals,?
Show that x cubed plus two x minus seven equals zero can be rearranged to x equals ∛(seven minus two x).
x0 equals one and xn plus one equals ∛(three minus xn). Find x2, to four decimal places.
x0 equals zero and xn plus one equals (xn cubed plus one) divided by five. This is a rearrangement of x cubed minus five x plus one equals zero. Find x2, to four decimal places.
Show that x squared minus six x minus two equals zero can be rearranged to x equals six plus the fraction two over x,.
x0 equals four and xn plus one equals four plus the fraction three over xn,. This comes from x squared minus four x minus three equals zero. Find x3, to three decimal places.

Key idea: to prove a solution to n decimal places, test the number half a unit of the last decimal place below your answer and the number half a unit above it. For two decimal places, that is zero point zero zero five either side. A change of sign proves the answer.
x0 equals one and xn plus one equals ∛(three minus xn). Find x5, to two decimal places.

x0 equals one point five and xn plus one equals ∛(seven minus two xn). Use iteration to find the solution of x cubed plus two x minus seven equals zero, to two decimal places. Keep going until two terms in a row agree to two decimal places.
f of x equals x cubed plus x minus three. Work out f of (one point two zero five), to three decimal places. (This is one of the two checks for the solution one point two one to two decimal places.)

For f of x equals x cubed plus x minus three, f of (one point two zero five) equals minus zero point zero four five and f of (one point two one five) equals zero point zero zero nine. What can you say about the solution?
x0 equals zero and xn plus one equals (xn cubed plus one) divided by five. Use iteration to find the solution of x cubed minus five x plus one equals zero, to three decimal places.
x0 equals four and xn plus one equals four plus the fraction three over xn,. Use iteration to find a solution of x squared minus four x minus three equals zero, to two decimal places.
Key idea: a multiplier handles a percentage change, and then adding or taking away a fixed amount handles a payment. Do the multiplying first, then add or take away.

A loan balance is B0 equals three thousand. Each month one percent is added, and then two hundred and fifty pounds is paid. Bn plus one equals one point zero one Bn minus two hundred and fifty. Find B2, in pounds. Type it like one thousand, two hundred and thirty-four point five zero.

Same loan: B0 equals three thousand and Bn plus one equals one point zero one Bn minus two hundred and fifty. Find B5, to the nearest penny. Type it like one thousand, two hundred and thirty-four point five zero.
Same loan: B0 equals three thousand and Bn plus one equals one point zero one Bn minus two hundred and fifty. After how many months is the balance first below one thousand pounds?

A savings account adds three percent each year, and then one hundred pounds is paid in. Sn plus one equals one point zero three Sn plus one hundred, with S0 equals five hundred. Find S3, to the nearest penny. Type it like one thousand, two hundred and thirty-four point five zero.

A plumber's van costs twenty-four thousand pounds and loses fifteen percent of its value each year. Vn plus one equals zero point eight five Vn, with V0 equals twenty-four thousand. Find V3, in pounds.
Why does the loan rule Bn plus one equals one point zero one Bn minus two hundred and fifty have both times one point zero one and minus two hundred and fifty?

Key idea: if the terms settle at L, then putting L into the rule gives L back. So L equals f of L. Solve that equation to find the exact value the terms settle at. And, going the other way, an iterative formula tells you which equation it is solving.
xn plus one equals three xn minus two and x2 equals twenty-five. Work backwards to find x1.
The terms of xn plus one equals (xn plus twelve) divided by four settle at a number L. Solve L equals (L plus twelve) divided by four to find L.

The terms of xn plus one equals square root of (xn plus six) (starting at x0 equals one) settle at a number L, so L equals square root of (L plus six). Square both sides, solve the quadratic, and give the positive value of L.
The formula xn plus one equals ∛(seven minus two xn) is used to solve an equation. Which equation is it?
x0 equals three and xn plus one equals two xn minus three. Find x5. (Work out the first few terms and look at what happens.)

Priya says: for f of x equals the fraction one over x,, f of minus one equals minus one and f of one equals one. The sign changes, so f of x equals zero has a solution between minus one and one. What is wrong?

Sam says: I tried xn plus one equals three minus xn cubed with x0 equals one point two for x cubed plus x minus three equals zero. The terms were one point two seven, zero point nine four, two point one six, minus seven point one four. They run away, so the equation has no solution. What is wrong?

Lee says: I want the solution of x cubed plus x minus three equals zero to two decimal places. I used xn plus one equals ∛(three minus xn) and rounded each answer to one decimal place before using it again. I got one point three, one point two, one point two, one point two, so the answer is one point two zero. What went wrong?
x0 equals one point five and xn plus one equals ∛(seven minus two xn). Find x2, to four decimal places.

f of x equals x cubed plus two x minus seven. You are given f of (one point five) equals minus zero point six two five. Work out f of (one point six), to three decimal places. What does it tell you about the solution of x cubed plus two x minus seven equals zero?
Which is a correct rearrangement of x squared minus x minus five equals zero into x equals,?
x0 equals two and xn plus one equals square root of (xn plus five). Find x3, to three decimal places.

f of x equals x cubed minus five x plus one. You are given f of (zero point two) equals zero point zero zero eight. Work out f of (zero point two one), to three decimal places. What does the change of sign tell you?

A savings account adds three percent each year, and then one hundred pounds is paid in. Sn plus one equals one point zero three Sn plus one hundred, with S0 equals five hundred. After how many years is the balance first above one thousand pounds?

A joiner takes a four thousand, eight hundred pounds loan for tools. Each month one point five percent interest is added to the balance, and then three hundred pounds is paid. Bn plus one equals one point zero one five Bn minus three hundred, with B0 equals four thousand, eight hundred. Find B3, the balance after three months, to the nearest penny. Type it like one thousand, two hundred and thirty-four point five zero.
Same loan: B0 equals four thousand, eight hundred and Bn plus one equals one point zero one five Bn minus three hundred. After how many months is the balance first below three thousand pounds?

An electrician tests a cable under load. A simple model for its temperature T (in degrees Celsius) after each ten minutes is Tn plus one equals zero point nine Tn plus eight, with T0 equals twenty. Find T3, to one decimal place.
In the same cable model, Tn plus one equals zero point nine Tn plus eight. The temperature settles at a value L. Put L in place of both Tn and Tn plus one and solve to find L, in degrees Celsius.

A plumber is checking a hot water cylinder that is being switched off. A simple model for its temperature T (in degrees Celsius) after each hour is Tn plus one equals zero point eight eight Tn plus two point four, with T0 equals sixty. Find T3, to one decimal place.

In the cylinder model, Tn plus one equals zero point eight eight Tn plus two point four. The temperature settles at a value L. Solve L equals zero point eight eight L plus two point four to find L, in degrees Celsius. Is the answer sensible for a room?
x0 equals one point five and xn plus one equals ∛(seven minus two xn). Work out x3. Give your answer to three decimal places.

f of x equals x cubed minus five x plus one. (a) Show that f of x equals zero has a root between zero point two and zero point three. (b) Use xn plus one equals (xn cubed plus one) divided by five with x0 equals zero point two to find this root to three decimal places. Type your answer to part (b).

A loan balance is Bn pounds after n months. Bn plus one equals one point zero one Bn minus two hundred and fifty and B0 equals three thousand. Work out after how many months the balance first falls below five hundred pounds.
The iteration xn plus one equals square root of (xn plus two) settles at a number L. Show that L equals two.
f of x equals x cubed plus x minus three. Show that the solution of f of x equals zero is one point two one to two decimal places.

xn plus one equals the fraction one over one plus xn, with x0 equals one gives the terms zero point five, zero point six six seven, zero point six, zero point six two five, zero point six one five, zero point six one nine,. They settle at a number L. Write L equals the fraction one over one plus L,, rearrange it to a quadratic equal to zero, and use the quadratic formula to find L, to three decimal places.

f of x equals x cubed minus three x plus one. Work out f of minus two, f of minus one, f of zero, f of one and f of two. Use them to show that f of x equals zero has three solutions, and give an interval of width one for each. The picture shows: A curve on axes with five dots marked at x equal to minus two, minus one, zero, one and two. The curve is smooth with no gaps.
f of x equals the fraction one over x, has f of minus one equals minus one and f of one equals one. Does f of x equals zero have a solution between minus one and one? Type yes or no.

xn plus one equals (xn plus the fraction seven over xn,) divided by two with x0 equals three settles at a number L. Find x3, to five decimal places. Then show that L equals square root of seven: put L in place of xn and xn plus one and solve.
A few questions use a letter such as x for a number we do not know yet. Treat it as a blank box: x plus two x equals three x means one box plus two boxes. Algebra basics explains it fully.

The temperature is minus four degrees Celsius and rises by nine degrees. What is the new temperature in degrees Celsius? The picture shows: A vertical thermometer scale from minus ten to ten degrees with the starting temperature of minus four degrees marked. The temperature then rises by nine degrees.
Work out seven times nine.

Key idea: bigger numbers are further to the right. So minus two is bigger than minus ten, even though ten looks bigger than two. A debt (money you owe) of two pounds is better than a debt of ten pounds. (£ means pounds, the UK money.)
Which is the biggest: minus seven, minus two or minus ten? The picture shows: A number line from minus ten to zero with the three numbers minus ten, minus seven and minus two marked.
Which is the smaller number: minus eight or minus three?
What number is halfway between minus six and two? The picture shows: A number line from minus eight to four with minus six and two marked. The number halfway between them is not marked.
How far is minus three from four on the number line? The picture shows: A number line from minus five to six with minus three and four marked. The distance between them is the question.
What is three more than minus five?
Key idea: start at the first number, then move. minus three plus five: start at minus three, go up five, land on two. minus four minus three: start at minus four, go down three, land on minus seven.
Work out minus three plus five. The picture shows: A number line from minus six to six with the starting point minus three marked. Adding five means moving five steps to the right.
Work out minus four minus three. The picture shows: A number line from minus ten to two with the starting point minus four marked. Subtracting three means moving three steps to the left.
Work out two minus seven. The picture shows: A number line from minus eight to four with the starting point two marked. Subtracting seven means moving seven steps to the left, past zero.
Work out minus six plus ten.

The temperature is three degrees Celsius and falls by eight degrees. What is the new temperature in degrees Celsius? The picture shows: A vertical thermometer scale from minus ten to ten degrees with the starting temperature of three degrees marked. The temperature then falls by eight degrees.
Key idea: subtracting a debt makes you richer. If someone takes away a three pounds debt of yours, you are three pounds better off. So five minus (minus three) is five plus three.
Work out five minus (minus three).
Work out minus two minus (minus six).
A player has three points. A trap adds minus five points. What is the score now?
Work out minus four minus (minus four).
Work out seven minus (minus two) plus (minus three).

Key idea: for example, (minus five) times (minus six) has the same signs, so the answer is positive: thirty. And three times (minus four) has different signs, so the answer is negative: minus twelve. Division undoes multiplication, so it follows the same rule (for non-zero numbers; you cannot divide by zero).
A quiz game takes away four points for each wrong answer. Zara gets three answers wrong. What is the change in her score?
Work out (minus five) times (minus six).
Work out minus twenty-four divided by six.
Work out minus twenty divided by (minus four).
Work out (minus two) times five times (minus three).
Work out (minus three) times (minus three).
Key idea: to find a missing number, undo what was done to it. Adding undoes subtracting. Multiplying undoes dividing. The signs look strange, but the method is the same.
minus seven plus? equals three. Find the missing number.
? minus (minus four) equals nine. Find the missing number.
(minus three) times? equals eighteen. Find the missing number.

The temperature rises from minus five degrees Celsius to eight degrees Celsius. By how many degrees did it rise? The picture shows: A vertical thermometer scale from minus six to ten degrees with minus five degrees and eight degrees marked. The size of the rise between them is the question.
? divided by (minus two) equals six. Find the missing number.

Key idea: the difference between two values is the higher one minus the lower one. From minus thirty metres to one hundred and fifty metres is one hundred and fifty minus (minus thirty) equals one hundred and eighty metres.

What is the balance in pounds? The picture shows: A vertical scale from minus sixty to one hundred and forty pounds. The starting balance of minus forty-five pounds, which is overdrawn, is marked. Then one hundred and twenty pounds is paid in.

A shipwreck is thirty metres below sea level (minus thirty metres). A cliff is one hundred and fifty metres above sea level. How many metres higher is the cliff than the wreck? The picture shows: A vertical scale in metres with sea level at zero. A shipwreck is marked at minus thirty metres and the top of a cliff at one hundred and fifty metres. The height difference between them is the question.
Find the next number in the sequence minus eight, minus five, minus two,,

A lift (elevator) goes from floor minus two (a basement, below the ground) to floor five. How many floors does it travel? The picture shows: A vertical scale of floors from minus three to six with floor minus two (the basement) and floor five marked. The number of floors between them is the question.

The temperatures one day were minus three, four, minus eight and zero degrees. What is the range (highest minus lowest)? The picture shows: A vertical scale from minus ten to six degrees with the four temperatures minus three, four, minus eight and zero marked.
Ben says: minus three minus four equals one. What went wrong?
Cara says: (minus two) times (minus five) equals minus ten. What went wrong?
Dan says: five minus (minus two) equals three. What went wrong?
A football team has a goal difference of minus eight. After a win, it goes up by three. What is the goal difference now?
Work out six minus (minus six).
Work out (minus two) times (minus two) times (minus two).
Which is the biggest: minus zero point five, minus zero point zero five or minus five?
Work out minus twelve divided by (minus three) times (minus two).

By how many degrees did the temperature rise from Monday to Tuesday? The picture shows: A vertical scale from minus six to six degrees with Monday at minus three degrees and Tuesday at four degrees marked.

Work out the range of the five minimum temperatures. The picture shows: A vertical scale from minus eight to six degrees with the five temperatures minus six, minus two, three, one and minus four marked.

A submarine at minus one hundred and twenty metres rises forty-five metres. What is its new depth in metres? Type it with a minus sign. The picture shows: A vertical scale in metres with sea level at zero. A submarine is marked at minus one hundred and twenty metres. It then rises forty-five metres.
Two numbers multiply to give minus twelve and add to give one. What is the larger of the two?

In this magic square every row, every column and both long diagonals add up to the same total (you are not told what it is). Find the number x in the bottom-left corner. The picture shows: A grid of three rows and three columns. Top row: minus three, blank, one. Middle row: blank, zero, blank. Bottom row: x, minus two, three. Every row, column and long diagonal has the same total.

Take any five whole numbers, positive or negative. Two of them must have a difference that is a multiple of four. (For example, minus three and five have difference eight.) Which is the key idea in the proof?

A student says: minus x is always negative. Check x equals three: minus x equals minus three. Check x equals five: minus x equals minus five. Both negative, so it is always true. Which sentence names the flaw?
A gamer starts with five coins and wins two coins on each of six levels. The total is five plus two times six. How many coins is that?
Work out six times seven.
Work out fifty-six minus nineteen.
Work out ninety divided by six.
Key idea: multiplication and division have equal priority. Addition and subtraction have equal priority. When operations have equal priority, work from left to right.
Work out seven plus two times four.
Work out twenty minus six divided by two.
A player has ten lives, loses two and then wins three back. Work out ten minus two plus three.
Work out eight divided by two times four.
A playlist has five songs. You add six albums of three songs each, then delete four songs. Work out five plus six times three minus four.

Key idea: a power belongs only to the number just before it. In two times three squared the square belongs to the three. So three squared equals nine first, then two times nine equals eighteen. To square both numbers, use brackets: (two times three) squared equals thirty-six.
Zoe mixes two batches of paint. Each batch has five millilitres of red and three millilitres of blue. Work out two times (five plus three), the total amount of paint in millilitres.
Work out (twelve minus four) divided by two.
Work out three plus two squared.
Work out (three plus two) squared.
Work out two times three squared.
Work out the fraction twelve plus eight over four,.
Key idea: you can go forwards (work out the answer). You can go backwards (decide where the brackets go, or find a missing number). Going backwards also checks a calculation.
Where must the brackets go to make two plus three times four equals twenty?
Which operation sign, in place of the?, makes six? two plus three equals six true?
three times (? plus two) equals twenty-one. Find the missing number.
? divided by four plus one equals six. Find the missing number.
Leo works out the total for a relay kit as nine plus eighteen divided by three and gets nine. What is the correct answer?
Ali says: six plus four times two equals twenty. What went wrong?
Bea says: twelve divided by three times two equals two. What went wrong?
Cal says: three squared equals six. What went wrong?
Work out seven plus three times (eight minus two).
Work out fifty minus three squared times two.
Work out two squared plus three squared.
Work out (ten minus four) squared divided by three.
Work out thirty-six divided by (two plus four) times three.
Work out three plus four times five squared.
Work out (twelve minus three) squared divided by three.
Sam works out six plus eighteen divided by three and gets eight. What is the correct answer?
Work out the fraction two plus ten over three, plus four times two.
Work out two times three squared divided by six plus (minus one).

A classic puzzle: use four four s, once each, with the usual operations and brackets, to make a target number. For example, four times four plus four divided by four equals seventeen. Which sign goes in the gap marked [ ] to make four times four [ ] (four divided by four) equals fifteen?
Work out minus three squared, using the standard order of operations.
Work out minus two squared plus (minus two) squared.
When x equals six, work out the value of (one over two)x (half of x).

Tonight: twenty minutes together Open Find my gaps and do it together. It is eleven questions and there is no pass mark. Then start on Ratio or Algebra basics, whichever one Find my gaps points to. Stop when your child is tired. One thing to say: What is it asking you to find?
What is it asking? What do you know? Tell me out loud.
Increase two hundred pounds by five percent. Answer in pounds.
What multiplier increases an amount by twelve percent? Give it as a decimal.
After a twenty percent discount a coat costs forty-eight pounds. What was the original price? Answer in pounds.
A price rises from forty pounds to forty-six pounds. What is the percentage increase? Give your answer like twelve percent.

Key idea: n changes of the same percentage means multiplier to the power of n. It does NOT mean multiplying the percentage by n. Three rises of four percent are not a twelve percent rise: it is one point zero four cubed equals one point one two four eight six four, a rise of twelve point four eight six four percent.
one thousand pounds grows by five percent each year. Which calculation gives the amount after three years?

one thousand pounds is invested at five percent compound interest for two years. How much is it worth? Give your answer in pounds, like four point five zero. The picture shows: Three boxes joined by two arrows. The first box says one thousand pounds. Each arrow says multiply by one point zero five. The other two boxes show a question mark.

eight hundred pounds is invested at three percent compound interest for three years. How much is it worth? Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny, like one hundred and twenty-three point four five.
Zara invests five hundred pounds at four percent compound interest for two years. How much interest does she earn altogether? Give your answer in pounds, like four point five zero.
A town of twelve thousand people grows by two percent each year. How many people live there after five years? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
A game starts with five thousand players. The number of players grows by ten percent every week. How many players are there after three weeks?
two thousand pounds is saved at five percent for two years. How many pounds more interest does compound interest give than simple interest? Give your answer in pounds.

Key idea: a multiplier above one is an increase and below one is a decrease. one point three two is a thirty-two percent increase. zero point eight five is a fifteen percent decrease. To find the percentage change, work out how far the multiplier is from one and write that as a percentage.
A phone's battery life goes from two hundred and fifty minutes to two hundred and ninety minutes. What is the percentage increase? Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
A coat is reduced from four hundred pounds to three hundred and forty pounds. What is the percentage decrease? Give your answer like twelve percent.
The population of a village goes from two thousand, four hundred to three thousand. What is the percentage increase? Give your answer like twelve percent.
A rent rises by ten percent and then, a year later, by another twenty percent. What is the overall percentage increase? Give your answer like twelve percent.
A price rises by twenty percent and then falls by twenty percent. What is the overall change?
Show that a price that rises by ten percent each year for two years has risen by twenty-one percent overall. Type the overall percentage increase you find, like twelve percent.
A price rises by four percent and then falls by two percent. What is the overall percentage change, to two decimal places? Give your answer like one point two five percent.

Key idea: a loss of ten percent a year does NOT mean a loss of twenty percent after two years. Each year you lose ten percent of what is left, which is a little less each time. Use zero point nine to the power of n.

A one thousand pounds scooter loses ten percent of its value each year. What is it worth after two years? Answer in pounds. The picture shows: Three boxes joined by two arrows. The first box says one thousand pounds. Each arrow says multiply by zero point nine. The other two boxes show a question mark.
What multiplier shows a loss of eight percent each year? Give it as a decimal.
A van is worth five thousand pounds. It loses twenty percent of its value each year. What is it worth after two years? Answer in pounds.
A laptop is worth nine hundred pounds. It loses thirty percent of its value in year one, and then ten percent of its value in year two. What is it worth after two years? Answer in pounds.

A guitar worth four hundred and fifty pounds depreciates by six percent each year. What is it worth after four years? Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny, like one hundred and twenty-three point four five.
A one thousand pounds tablet loses ten percent of its value each year. After how many whole years is it first worth less than seven hundred pounds?
A car loses ten percent of its value each year. After two years, how much of its original value has it lost?

Key idea: to undo n changes, divide by multiplier to the power of n. To find the rate when you know the start, the end and the number of years n, find the multiplier first: it is the n-th root of (end divided by start).

After two years at ten percent compound interest, an account holds one thousand, eight hundred and fifteen pounds. How much was paid in? Answer in pounds. The picture shows: Three boxes joined by two arrows. The first two boxes show a question mark. The last box says one thousand, eight hundred and fifteen pounds. Each arrow says multiply by one point one.
A van is worth six thousand, four hundred pounds after two years of twenty percent depreciation each year. What was its value when new? Answer in pounds.
After three years of ten percent growth each year, a town has thirteen thousand, three hundred and ten people. How many people lived there at the start?
eight hundred pounds grows to eight hundred and eighty-two pounds in two years at the same compound rate each year. What is the yearly rate? Give your answer like three percent.

A boat is worth ten thousand pounds and, two years later, eight thousand, one hundred pounds. It lost the same percentage of its value each year. What is that percentage? Give your answer like three percent.
three thousand pounds grows to three thousand, nine hundred and ninety-three pounds in three years at the same compound rate each year. What is the yearly rate? Give your answer like three percent.
one thousand pounds is invested at eight percent compound interest a year. After how many whole years is it first worth more than one thousand, five hundred pounds?
An account paid four percent compound interest each year for three years and now holds a known amount. How do you find the amount paid in?
Zoe says: two thousand pounds at five percent compound interest for three years is two thousand times one point one five equals two thousand, three hundred pounds. What went wrong?
Leo says: a van loses twenty percent of its value in each of two years, so it has lost forty percent of its value. What went wrong?
Increase two hundred and fifty pounds by twelve percent. Answer in pounds.
four hundred pounds is invested at three percent compound interest for two years. What is it worth? Give your answer in pounds, like one hundred and twenty-three point four five.
A jacket costs seventy-two pounds in a twenty percent sale. What was the price before the sale? Answer in pounds.
A price goes from eighty pounds to sixty-eight pounds. What is the percentage decrease? Give your answer like twelve percent.
Write zero point zero four five as a percentage. Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
A car costs fifteen thousand pounds new. It loses eighteen percent of its value in the first year. What is it worth after the first year? Answer in pounds.
Work out the value of Dev's investment after three years. Give your answer in pounds to the nearest penny, like one hundred and twenty-three point four five.
How much interest has Dev earned in the three years? Give your answer in pounds, like one hundred and twenty-three point four five.
Work out the value of the car after three years. Give your answer in pounds, like one hundred and twenty-three point four five.
A price rises by five percent and then falls by ten percent. It is now one hundred and thirteen pounds forty. Work out the original price. Answer in pounds.
A price rises by ten percent. By what percentage must it then fall to return to the original? Give your answer to one decimal place, like twelve point five percent.

Account eigh pays six percent simple interest a year on one thousand pounds. Account B pays five percent compound interest a year on one thousand pounds. After how many whole years is account B first worth more than account eigh?
A price p rises by x percent and then falls by x percent. Which expression gives the final price?
After a price rises by x percent and then falls by x percent, the overall multiplier is one minus x squared /ten thousand. Use x equals thirty. What is the overall multiplier? Give it as a decimal.

Units and money one hundred pence equals one pounds, so eighty-five p equals eighty-five pence and one pounds twenty equals one hundred and twenty p. Round money to two decimal places: twenty-eight point eight five seven pounds becomes twenty-eight pounds eighty-six. Do not mix pounds and pence in one calculation. Use only one of them. VAT is twenty percent: add it by multiplying by one point two. Take it off again by dividing by one point two.
Simplify the fraction twenty-five over one hundred,. Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Work out the fraction one over five, of sixty.
Write zero point three five as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
Fill the gap: the fraction three over five, equals the fraction? over one hundred,. What number goes where the? is?
Key idea: the percent sign is a way of writing divided by one hundred. To go from a percentage to a decimal, divide by one hundred. To go back, multiply by one hundred.

The whole bar is one hundred percent. It is cut into equal parts and some are shaded. What percentage is shaded? Give your answer like twelve percent. The picture shows: A bar cut into ten equal parts. The first seven parts are shaded pink and the last three are white. The whole bar stands for one hundred percent.
Write zero point six as a percentage. Give your answer like twelve percent.
Write thirty-five percent as a decimal.
Write thirty-five percent as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
Write the fraction three over eight, as a percentage. Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
In a survey, nine out of twenty-five gamers chose a blue controller. What percentage chose blue? Give your answer like twelve percent.
Which is the biggest: zero point six, fifty-five percent or the fraction five over eight,?
Key idea: percentages add up. thirty-five percent equals ten percent plus ten percent plus ten percent plus five percent. Work out the ten percent once, then build the rest from it.
What is ten percent of eighty pounds?
What is twenty-five percent of sixty-four kilograms? Give your answer in kg.

The bar stands for one hundred and fifty pounds and is cut into ten equal parts. Four parts are shaded. How much money do the shaded parts stand for? Answer in pounds. The picture shows: A bar standing for one hundred and fifty pounds, cut into ten equal parts. The first four parts are shaded pink.
A game has two hundred and fifty levels. Kai has finished eighteen percent of them. How many levels has Kai finished? You can use a calculator.
A plumber's materials cost four hundred and eighty pounds. The copper pipe is thirty-five percent of the cost. How much does the pipe cost? Answer in pounds.
Use a calculator to work out seven point five percent of sixty-four pounds. Give your answer in pounds, like four point five zero.
Which calculation finds twelve percent of three hundred and fifty?

Key idea: the whole always goes in the denominator, and both amounts must be in the same units. sixty centimetres out of three metres needs a change to sixty centimetres out of three hundred centimetres first.
A team won six of their eight matches. What percentage did they win? Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
A cake mix weighs five hundred grams. seventy-five grams of it is cocoa. What percentage of the mix is cocoa? Give your answer like twelve percent.
Sam earns one hundred and fifty pounds a week and saves eighteen pounds. What percentage of the wage (the money Sam earns) does Sam save? Give your answer like twelve percent.
A cable is three metres long. A piece sixty centimetres long is cut off. What percentage of the cable is cut off? Give your answer like twelve percent.
In one quiz Maya got thirty-three out of forty. What percentage is that? Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
Who did best? Ali scored seventeen out of twenty. Bea scored thirty-three out of forty. Cat scored forty-one out of fifty.
Key idea: a percentage change is one multiplication. The multiplier is the percentage you end with, written as a decimal.
What single number do you multiply by to increase an amount by eight percent? Give it as a decimal, like one point two five.
What single number do you multiply by to decrease an amount by thirty percent? Give it as a decimal.
Increase fifty pounds by ten percent. Answer in pounds.
A bike costs two hundred and fifty pounds before VAT. VAT is twenty percent. What is the price with VAT? Answer in pounds.

A eighty-four pounds hoodie is twenty-five percent off in a sale. What is the sale price? Answer in pounds. The picture shows: A bar standing for eighty-four pounds cut into four equal parts. One part is shaded and marked as the twenty-five percent taken off.
A game has one thousand, two hundred players. The number of players falls by five percent. How many players are there now?
Which single multiplier decreases an amount by twelve percent?
Mia puts six hundred pounds in an account that pays three percent simple interest a year. How much interest does she earn in four years? Answer in pounds.

Key idea: after a percentage change, the new amount is a percentage of the original. Undo it by dividing by the multiplier. Never take the percentage off the new amount, because it was not taken from there.

Trainers cost sixty-three pounds in a twenty-five percent sale. What was the price before the sale? Answer in pounds. The picture shows: A bar cut into four equal parts. The original price is the whole bar and is not known. Three parts are shaded and together are the sixty-three pound sale price. The white part is the twenty-five percent taken off.
A boiler costs five hundred and forty pounds with twenty percent VAT included. What is the price without VAT? Answer in pounds.
A rent is now one thousand, two hundred and forty-eight pounds after a four percent rise. What was the rent before the rise? Answer in pounds.
A cereal packet says twenty percent extra free and now holds six hundred grams. How many grams did the normal packet hold?
A game had eight hundred players last month and one thousand players this month. What is the percentage increase? Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
An amplifier used to cost two hundred and fifty pounds. It now costs two hundred pounds. What is the percentage decrease? Give your answer like twelve percent.
A cafe's daily takings fell from six hundred and forty pounds to five hundred and sixty pounds. What is the percentage decrease? Give your answer like eight percent.
A shop takes thirty percent off its prices. You know a sale price. How do you find the original price?
Tom says: a coat costs forty-eight pounds after twenty percent off, so the original price was forty-eight pounds plus twenty percent equals fifty-seven pounds sixty. What went wrong?
Priya says: if a price goes up by ten percent and then comes down by ten percent, you are back where you started. What is wrong with that?
Which is smaller: the fraction three over eight, or forty percent?
Write zero point zero four as a percentage. Give your answer like twelve percent.
Without a calculator, work out seventeen point five percent of eighty pounds. Answer in pounds.
A train fare is thirty-six pounds. It rises by five percent. What is the new fare? Give your answer in pounds, like four point five zero.
A TV costs three hundred and forty pounds in a fifteen percent sale. What was the price before the sale? Answer in pounds.
In a music class, eighteen of the twenty-four students play guitar. What percentage play guitar? Give your answer like twelve percent.
A recipe uses two hundred and forty grams of butter. For a big batch you need one hundred and fifty percent of that amount. How many grams of butter is that?
Work out the sale price. Answer in pounds.
Work out the original price of the bike. Answer in pounds.

The shop paid two hundred and forty pounds for the bike. What is the shop's percentage profit on that cost when it sells the bike to Tia for two hundred and fifty-five pounds? Give your answer like twelve point five percent.
A price of one hundred pounds goes up by twenty percent and then goes down by twenty percent. Work out the final price. Answer in pounds.
A price rises by twenty-five percent. By what percentage must the new price fall to get back to the start? Give your answer like twelve point five percent. (Try starting with one hundred pounds.)
Without a calculator, find four percent of seventy-five. Here is a trick: four percent of seventy-five is the same as seventy-five percent of four.
Why is a percent of b always the same as b percent of a? For example, eight percent of twenty-five equals twenty-five percent of eight equals two.
A radio costs ninety-six pounds with twenty percent VAT included. How many pounds of the ninety-six pounds is VAT?
A boiler pressure valve costs eighty-four pounds fifty before VAT. VAT is twenty percent. How much does it cost including VAT, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.
A merchant gives a plumber fifteen percent trade discount on a basin listed at one hundred and thirty-two pounds. What does the plumber pay, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.

A plumber buys a tap for eighteen pounds fifty. She adds a thirty percent markup (a percentage added to what she paid), and then twenty percent VAT is added to her selling price. How much does the customer pay, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.

A plumber sells a shower valve for one hundred and twenty-six pounds fifty after adding a fifteen percent markup to what she paid. What did she pay, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.

A boiler service costs ninety-five pounds plus VAT at twenty percent. A landlord gets ten percent off the price before VAT. How much does the landlord pay in total, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.

The supply to a socket is two hundred and thirty volts. Along a long cable the voltage drops by five volts. What is the voltage drop as a percentage of two hundred and thirty volts? Give your answer to two decimal places, as a number without the percent sign.

An electrician buys forty metres of cable at one pounds eighty-five per metre before VAT. VAT is twenty percent. How much does the cable cost including VAT, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.
A salon buys shampoo for fourteen pounds fifty before VAT. VAT of twenty percent is added. What is the price including VAT? Type it like twelve point five zero.
A salon has eighty bottles of shampoo in stock. After a busy week the stock is down fifteen percent. How many bottles are left?
A cut and colour usually costs thirty-six pounds. Students get ten percent off. How much does a student pay? Type it like twelve point five zero.

Football boots cost eighty-five pounds. In a sale they are reduced by thirty percent. Club members then get a further ten percent off the sale price. How much does a club member pay? Type it like twelve point five zero.
A salon raises the price of a cut from twenty-eight pounds to thirty-one pounds fifty. Work out the percentage increase. Type the number only, like seven point five.

A gamer scores four thousand and eighty-two points. What is the value of the digit eight in that score? The picture shows: The number four thousand and eighty-two written in columns. From the left the columns are thousands, hundreds, tens and units, holding the digits four, zero, eight and two.
What is one more than three thousand and ninety-nine?
Work out ten times ten.
Work out ten times one hundred.

Key idea: the same digit is worth different amounts in different columns. The eight in four thousand and eighty-two is worth eighty. The eight in four thousand, eight hundred and two is worth eight hundred. The zero in four thousand and eighty-two is a spacer. Take it out and the four is only worth four hundred.

What is the value of the seven in three thousand, seven hundred and twenty-five? The picture shows: The number three thousand, seven hundred and twenty-five written in columns. From the left the columns are thousands, hundreds, tens and units, holding the digits three, seven, two and five.

A song's stream count is four thousands, zero hundreds, three tens and five units. Write the number of streams in digits. The picture shows: Four empty place value columns, from the left thousands, hundreds, tens and units. Each holds a question mark for the digit you need to write.

A fitness band shows four thousand and thirty steps. Write the number of steps in digits. The picture shows: Four empty place value columns, from the left thousands, hundreds, tens and units. Each holds a question mark for the digit you need to write.

How many tens are there in five hundred and sixty? The picture shows: A bar for the number five hundred and sixty. Inside the bar are the words each part is ten and a question mark for the number of parts.

Which is bigger: nine thousand and ninety-nine or nine thousand, one hundred and one? The picture shows: Two numbers written one above the other in the same four columns: thousands, hundreds, tens and units. The top row is nine thousand and ninety-nine. The bottom row is nine thousand, one hundred and one.

Key idea: compare decimals column by column from the left, not by how long the numbers look. Add zeros so both numbers have the same number of decimal places: zero point four zero and zero point three five. Now forty beats thirty-five, so zero point four is bigger than zero point three five.

What is the value of the five in three point two five four? The picture shows: The number three point two five four in columns: a units column, then after the decimal point three more columns. Each column holds one digit.
Write zero point seven as a fraction.

How many hundredths are there in zero point six? The picture shows: The number zero point six in columns: a units column holding zero, then after the decimal point two more columns. Each column holds one digit.
Write three plus the fraction two over ten, plus the fraction five over one hundred, as a decimal.
Which of these is the biggest: zero point four, zero point three seven or zero point three nine nine?

Key idea: multiplying by ten moves every digit one place left. Dividing by ten moves every digit one place right. For one hundred, move two places. For one thousand, move three. Zeros fill the empty columns.

Work out three point four times one hundred. The picture shows: The number three point four in columns: units three and tenths four, with the hundreds and tens columns empty to its left. Multiplying by one hundred moves each digit two columns to the left.

A fan page has five thousand, six hundred likes shared evenly across one hundred posts. Work out five thousand, six hundred divided by one hundred, the likes per post. The picture shows: The number five thousand, six hundred in columns: thousands five, hundreds six, tens zero, units zero. Dividing by one hundred moves each digit two columns to the right.
A game gives you zero point zero seven coins for every click. You click one thousand times. How many coins do you get?

Work out two point five divided by one thousand. The picture shows: The number two point five in columns: units two and tenths five, with hundredths and thousandths empty. Dividing by one thousand moves each digit three columns to the right.

Key idea: only the digit immediately to the right of your column decides. Find the column you are rounding to. Look at the next digit to its right. If it is five or more, round up. If it is four or less, keep the digit as it is. Example: round three thousand, four hundred and sixty-eight to the nearest one hundred. The hundreds column holds the four. The next digit is six, so the four goes up to five. The answer is three thousand, five hundred.

Round four thousand, eight hundred and sixty-two to the nearest one hundred. The picture shows: A number line with four thousand, eight hundred at the left end and four thousand, nine hundred at the right end, and a small tick halfway between. A dot marks four thousand, eight hundred and sixty-two.

Round six point seven four nine to one decimal place. The picture shows: A number line with six point seven at the left end and six point eight at the right end, and a small tick halfway at six point seven five. A dot marks six point seven four nine.

A song has fifteen thousand, six hundred and fifty streams. Round the streams to the nearest one thousand. The picture shows: A number line with fifteen thousand at the left end and sixteen thousand at the right end, and a small tick halfway. A dot marks fifteen thousand, six hundred and fifty.
Round zero point zero five two seven to one significant figure.

Round three point nine nine six to two decimal places. The picture shows: A number line with three point nine nine at the left end and four point zero zero at the right end, and a small tick halfway at three point nine nine five. A dot marks three point nine nine six.

Round seven thousand, three hundred and fifty to the nearest one hundred. The picture shows: A number line with seven thousand, three hundred at the left end and seven thousand, four hundred at the right end. A dot marks seven thousand, three hundred and fifty.
Key idea: doing a calculation forwards and then backwards through the same columns checks that you understand how the columns work.
A number multiplied by ten gives three hundred and forty. What is the number?
A number divided by one hundred gives zero point five six. What is the number?
What is the smallest whole number that rounds to forty when rounded to the nearest ten? The picture shows: A number line with thirty, forty and fifty labelled.
What is the largest whole number that rounds to forty when rounded to the nearest ten? The picture shows: A number line with thirty, forty and fifty labelled.
A number rounded to one decimal place is two point five. Which of these could be the original number?
Ravi says: three point four five is bigger than three point five, because forty-five is bigger than five. What went wrong?
Zoe says: six point zero seven times ten equals six point seven zero. What went wrong?

Round fifty-two thousand, six hundred and eighty-four to the nearest one thousand. The picture shows: A number line with fifty-two thousand at the left end and fifty-three thousand at the right end, and a small tick halfway. A dot marks fifty-two thousand, six hundred and eighty-four.

What is the value of the five in fifty-two thousand, six hundred and eighty-four? The picture shows: The number fifty-two thousand, six hundred and eighty-four written in five columns, with a column name above each digit.
Work out zero point zero zero four eight times one thousand.
Which is the smallest of zero point five, zero point zero five, zero point five zero five and zero point five five? Type the number.
Which of these is closest to one thousand?
Write the number of people to the nearest thousand.

Write down the value of the digit six in fifty-two thousand, six hundred and eighty-four. The picture shows: The number fifty-two thousand, six hundred and eighty-four written in five columns, with a column name above each digit.
Estimate forty-eight point seven times nineteen point eight by rounding each number to one significant figure.
Round zero point zero four five six seven to two significant figures.

A number rounds to three thousand, four hundred to the nearest one hundred. What is the largest whole number it could be? The picture shows: A number line with three thousand, three hundred, three thousand, four hundred and three thousand, five hundred labelled.
Why mixed? Picking the method is half the skill, and a few minutes a day works better than one long session.

Writing probabilities Write a probability as a fraction, a decimal or a percentage: the fraction one over four,, zero point two five or twenty-five percent. A probability is never less than zero and never more than one. If you get one point two, something has gone wrong. Give fractions in their simplest form unless the question says otherwise.
Simplify the fraction eight over twenty,. Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Work out one minus the fraction three over eight,. Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Work out the fraction one over four, plus the fraction one over two,. Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Work out the fraction two over five, of thirty.
Key idea: a probability is a Fraction, a Decimal or a Percentage between zero and one (or zero percent and one hundred percent). It can never be negative and never be bigger than one.
Which of these could not be a probability?
A bag holds only red counters. You take one without looking. What is the probability that it is red? Type a number.
A forecast says there is a thirty-five percent chance of rain. Write this probability as a decimal.
A normal dice has faces one to six. What is the probability that it shows a seven? Type a number.

The marker shows the probability that a train is on time. What decimal does it show? The picture shows: A number line from zero to one with ten equal gaps. A pink marker sits on one of the ticks, marked with a question mark.
Which of these probabilities shows the most likely outcome?

Key idea: count the equal sectors, not the different numbers. The denominator of the fraction is the total number of sectors (eight on this spinner), and the numerator is the number of sectors you want.

One counter is taken at random from the bag shown. What is the probability that it is blue? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five. The picture shows: Ten counters: three marked R, five marked B and two marked G.
A fair dice is rolled. What is the probability that the score is a prime number? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

The spinner shown is fair. What is the probability that it lands on four? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five. The picture shows: A spinner cut into six equal sectors labelled two, four, four, five, seven and nine.

A raffle (a prize draw where people buy numbered tickets) sells two hundred tickets. Dev buys eight of them. One ticket is drawn at random to win. What is the probability that Dev wins? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

A standard pack has fifty-two cards in four suits of thirteen cards each (hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades). One card is picked at random. What is the probability that it is a heart? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
A spinner has three colours, so Sam says the probability of red equals the fraction one over three,. When is Sam right?
Key idea: all the probabilities of all the possible outcomes add up to one. If you know every probability except one, subtract the others from one.
The probability that a train is late is zero point one five. What is the probability that it is on time?
The probability that Mia wins a game is the fraction three over seven,. What is the probability that she does not win? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
The probability that a tile in a box is cracked is six percent. What is the probability it is not cracked? Give your answer like twelve percent.
The table gives the probability of each colour that a spinner can land on. The probabilities add up to one. What is the probability that it lands on green? Give a decimal.

A bag has four red, six yellow and five white counters. One counter is taken at random. What is the probability that it is not yellow? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

Aled says that for Saturday's match the probability of win equals zero point six, the probability of draw equals zero point three and the probability of lose equals zero point two. Why cannot this be right?
Key idea: list the outcomes in a fixed order so you do not miss any. For two dice there are six times six equals thirty-six equally likely pairs, and the table shows the total score for each pair.
Two coins are tossed. List every possible pair, like HH and HT. How many different outcomes are there? Count HT and TH as different.
Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of two heads? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
A cafe meal deal is one sandwich (cheese, ham or egg) and one drink (tea or juice). How many different meal deals are there?
Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are added. Use the table above. What is the probability that the total is nine? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

A fair spinner has three equal sectors eigh, B and C. The spinner is spun once and a fair coin is tossed once. What is the probability that the spinner lands on B and the coin lands on tails? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Two fair dice are rolled and the scores are added. What is the probability that the total score is less than five? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
Key idea: an expected number is what happens on average, not a promise. A fair coin tossed ten times is expected to give five heads, but four or six would not surprise anyone.
A fair dice is rolled one hundred and twenty times. How many times do you expect it to show a five?
The probability of rain on a day in April is zero point three. April has thirty days. How many rainy days do you expect?
Dev drops a drawing pin fifty times. It lands point up eighteen times. What is the relative frequency of point up? Give a decimal.

A factory tests eight hundred phone screens and finds that twenty-four are faulty. Use this to estimate the probability that a screen is faulty. Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
The factory makes five thousand screens. Using the estimate the probability of faulty equals the fraction three over one hundred,, how many faulty screens do you expect?

Three students each toss the same coin and count the heads. Ali: seven heads in ten tosses. Bea: forty-six heads in one hundred tosses. Cat: five hundred and twelve heads in one thousand tosses. Whose result gives the best estimate of the probability of heads?

A biased spinner has the probability of red equals zero point four and the probability of blue equals zero point three five. The only other colour is green. The spinner is spun two hundred times. How many greens do you expect?

Key idea: you may only add the probabilities when the outcomes cannot happen together. Even and bigger than three can both be true (four and six), so adding their probabilities would count four and six twice.
A fair dice is rolled. What is the probability that it shows a two or a five? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

A student picks one flavour of crisps at random. the probability of salt equals zero point three five, the probability of cheese equals zero point two five and the probability of other equals zero point four. What is the probability of salt or cheese?

A bag has four red, seven blue and nine green counters. One counter is picked at random. What is the probability that it is a red or a green counter? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
A fair dice is rolled once. Which pair of outcomes is mutually exclusive?

A card is picked at random from a standard pack of fifty-two cards. There are four kings and four queens. What is the probability it is a king or a queen? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
A fair dice is rolled. What is the probability of an even number or a number bigger than three? List the scores that fit. Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
Key idea: or adds (for outcomes that cannot happen together). and multiplies (for independent events). A probability never gets bigger when you multiply it by another probability.
A fair coin is tossed and a fair dice is rolled. What is the probability of heads and a six? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Zoe is late for school with probability zero point one on any day, independently. What is the probability that she is late on both Monday and Tuesday?
A seed grows with probability zero point eight. Two seeds are planted and they grow independently. What is the probability that both grow?
Which pair of events is independent?
Use the table of forty students above. One student is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is a boy who goes by bus? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
Use the same table. One of the girls is chosen at random. What is the probability that she walks? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

A part from machine eigh is faulty with probability zero point zero two. A part from machine B is faulty with probability zero point zero five. The machines work independently. What is the probability that both parts are faulty?

A biased coin lands on heads with probability zero point six. The tree shows two tosses. What probability goes in place of the question mark? The picture shows: A tree diagram for two tosses. The first toss has heads zero point six and tails marked with a question mark. The second toss has heads zero point six and tails zero point four after each first result.

Two seeds are planted. Each grows (G) with probability zero point eight, independently. What is the probability that exactly one seed grows? The picture shows: A tree diagram for two seeds. Each seed grows (G) with probability zero point eight or does not grow (N) with probability zero point two.
A seed fails to grow with probability zero point two. Two seeds are planted independently. What is the probability that neither grows?

A factory tests two parts. Each part is faulty with probability zero point one, independently. What is the probability that at least one part is faulty? (Try finding the probability of none faulty first.)
How do you find the probability of a whole path on a tree diagram, such as first this, then that?

A bus is late with probability the fraction one over five, each day, independently. What is the probability that it is late on exactly one of two days? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
On a two-stage tree diagram, what do the probabilities of all the end results add up to?
Key idea: on a tree diagram for picking without replacement, the second-stage probabilities are different on each branch. Work out each one from what is left in the bag.

A bag has four red and six yellow counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

The tree shows two counters taken without replacement from a bag of three red and two blue. What fraction goes where the question mark is? The picture shows: A tree diagram for taking two counters from a bag of three red (R) and two blue (B) without putting the first back. First pick: red three over five, blue two over five. Second pick after red: red?, blue two over four. Second pick after blue: red three over four, blue one over four.

A bag has three red and two blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement. What is the probability of one red and one blue, in either order? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.

A box has eight screws and three of them are damaged. Two screws are taken at random without replacement. What is the probability that neither is damaged? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
Two counters are taken from a bag without replacement. Why is the second probability different from the first?

A pack has ten cards and four of them are rare. Two cards are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is rare? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five. (Try finding the probability of no rare card first.)

Key idea: fill in the overlap first. Then take it away from the total of each set to find the only regions. Finally, the number outside is the total for the whole group minus everything inside the circles.

The Venn diagram shows twenty people. eigh is the set of people who own a bike and B is the set who own a skateboard. How many people are in set B altogether? The picture shows: Two overlapping circles eigh and B in a rectangle. A only holds eight, both holds four, B only holds six and two are outside both circles.

In the same Venn diagram (twenty people), one person is chosen at random. What is the probability that they are in neither set? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five. The picture shows: Two overlapping circles eigh and B in a rectangle. A only holds eight, both holds four, B only holds six and two are outside both circles.
In a group of forty pupils, twenty-two own a bike, fifteen own a skateboard and eight own both. How many own neither?

In a class of twenty-five, fourteen study French and nine study Spanish. The diagram shows that three study both. How many study only French? The picture shows: Two overlapping circles, French and Spanish, in a rectangle. The overlap holds three. The French only, Spanish only and outside regions are marked with question marks.

The letters p, q, r and s mark the four regions of a Venn diagram. Which letter marks the region that is in both eigh and B? Type the letter. The picture shows: Two overlapping circles eigh and B in a rectangle. The four regions are marked p (eigh only), q (the overlap), r (B only) and s (outside both).

In a class of thirty, seventeen like pasta, fourteen like pizza and six like both. One student is chosen at random. What is the probability that they like neither? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
Key idea: number wanted equals probability times total. So the total equals number wanted divided by probability. Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by it flipped over.
A bag has red and blue counters. the probability of red equals the fraction one over four, and there are five red counters. How many counters are in the bag?
The probability that a part is faulty is zero point zero four. In a batch you expect twenty-five faulty parts. How many parts are in the batch?
A bag has twenty-four counters. the probability of green equals the fraction three over eight,. How many green counters are in the bag?
A bag has three red counters, five blue counters and some green counters. the probability of green equals the fraction one over three,. How many green counters are there?
A bag has N counters. The probability that a counter taken at random is red is p. Which expression gives the number of red counters in the bag?
The probability that a bus is on time is zero point eight five. Out of forty buses, how many do you expect not to be on time?
Jo says: when I roll a fair dice there are three outcomes: a six, an even number and something else, so the probability of six equals the fraction one over three,. What is wrong?
Kit says: I tossed a fair coin five times and got heads every time, so the next toss is more likely to be tails. What is wrong?
Mia says: the probability of two heads when I toss two fair coins is the fraction one over two, plus the fraction one over two, equals one. What went wrong?
The probability that a switch is faulty is the fraction three over twenty,. Write this probability as a percentage. Give your answer like twelve percent.
A fair dice is rolled. What is the probability that the score is a multiple of three? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
The probability of a frost on a winter night is zero point one two. How many frosts do you expect in two hundred and fifty nights?
A fair coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of three heads? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
eigh and B are mutually exclusive events. the probability of eigh equals zero point three and the probability of B equals zero point five. What is the probability of eigh or B?

In a class of thirty, fourteen are boys. six of the boys and five of the girls wear glasses. A student is chosen at random. What is the probability that they wear glasses? Give your answer as a fraction, like three over five.
An electrician has a box of fifty fuses and three of them are faulty. She picks one at random. What is the probability that it is faulty? Type it as a fraction, like three over ten.

A valve fails a pressure test with probability zero point zero four. A plumber fits one hundred and fifty of these valves. Each failed valve costs thirty-eight pounds to replace. What is the expected cost, in pounds? Type it like forty-two point seven five.

A carpenter has a stack of twenty planks and four of them are warped. She picks one at random. What is the probability that it is not warped? Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form, like three over five.
An electrician tests two RCDs. Each passes the test with probability zero point nine eight, independently. What is the probability that both pass? Give a decimal.
A merchant finds that one in every forty taps sold is returned. A plumber orders four hundred taps. How many returns would you expect?
A roofer needs two dry days in a row. The probability of rain on any day is zero point two five, and the days are independent. What is the probability that both days are dry?
